about: Elmo Fire shows Sesame Street's Elmo with both arms thrown up in the air, grinning, while a wall of flames roars behind him on a black background. The contrast between the cheerful children's character and the apocalyptic inferno makes it the go-to picture for gleeful chaos: someone who started the fire, or who has fully accepted that everything is burning and is enjoying it. People also call it Hellmo or Elmo Rise, and animated versions are common as reaction GIFs whenever a situation spirals out of control.
origin: The figure was originally a crudely made Elmo decoration on a cake, shared on the Cake Wrecks blog in 2012. Internet users cut Elmo out of the photo and placed him in front of fire, and the edited version spread as a reaction image.
usage:
The top box sets the scene, usually "me" or "me when", and the bottom box names the disaster Elmo is presiding over. The joke works best when the speaker is either the cause of the chaos or happily indifferent to it, so phrase it as celebration rather than panic.

Good fits include deadline weeks, group chats exploding over drama, a game lobby falling apart, the office fridge after a holiday party, or the moment you decide to stop caring. The more mundane the trigger compared with the hellfire, the funnier it gets.
ideas: gives a penalty to the other team
